h: The Four Gifts and Their Divine Attributes
The divine names illuminate the four pathways of Torah, affliction, service, and prayer.

p: בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (מִשְׁפָּטִים פָּרָשָׁה ל):
In Midrash Rabbah (Mishpatim, Parashah 30):
שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיתֵּן לָהֶם אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים:
The Holy One, blessed be He, sought to give them four things:
תּוֹרָה, וְיִסּוּרִין, וַעֲבוֹדַת קָרְבָּנוֹת, וּתְפִלָּה;
Torah, afflictions, sacrificial service, and prayer;
וְלֹא בִּקְשׁוּ,
yet they did not desire them,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיֹּאמְרוּ לָאֵל סוּר מִמֶּנּוּ" – אֵלּוּ הַיִּסּוּרִין;
as it is said: "And they said unto God: Depart from us"—these are afflictions; "
וְדַעַת דְּרָכֶיךָ לֹא חָפָצְנוּ" – זֶה תּוֹרָה;
"And the knowledge of Your ways we do not desire"—this is Torah; "
מַה שַּׁדַּי כִּי נַעַבְדֶנּוּ" – אֵלּוּ הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת;
"What is the Almighty that we should serve Him?"—these are the sacrifices; "
וּמַה נּוֹעִיל כִּי נִפְגַּע בּוֹ" – זֶה תְּפִלָּה.
"And what profit should we have if we pray to Him?"—this is prayer.
זָכַר כָּאן בַּפָּסוּק שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת:
Scripture mentions here in the verse two Divine Names:
שֵׁם "אֵל" וְשֵׁם "שַׁדַּי",
the Name 'E-l' (אֵל) and the Name 'Shaddai' (שַׁדַּי),
שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא מֹשֶׁה
(345). both of them together have the gematria of Moshe (מֹשֶׁה = 345).
שֵׁם "אֵל" הוּא מִדַּת מַלְכוּת,
The Name 'E-l' corresponds to the attribute of Malchut,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, ח עַמּוּד א):
and as stated (Zohar Part I, 8a): "
כְּבוֹד כַּלָּה דְּאִקְרֵי אֵל, דִּכְתִיב: 'אֵל זֹעֵם בְּכָל יוֹם'";
‘the glory of the Bride which is called E-l, as it is written: "E-l has indignation every day"’;
וְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, צא עַמּוּד א):
and it is taught (Zohar Part II, 91a): "
נוּ״ן – רָזָא לְמִדְחַל מִקּוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
‘The letter Nun is the mystery of fearing the Holy One, blessed be He,
וּלְמִנְדַּע דְּאִית דִּין וְאִית דַּיָּין וְכוּלֵי וּפֻרְעָנוּתָא לְרַשִּׁיעַיָּא,
and knowing that there is judgment and a Judge, etc., and punishment for the wicked,
בְּגִין דְּרָזָא דִּילֵיהּ הֵ״א תַּתָּאָה",
because its mystery is the lower Hei’,
שֶׁמִּמִּדַּת מַלְכוּת הוּא הַדִּין,
for from the attribute of Malchut stems judgment, "
דִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא דִּינָא", כַּיָּדוּעַ.
'the law of the kingdom is law,' as is known.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "וַיֹּאמְרוּ לָאֵל סוּר מִמֶּנּוּ"
– And this is what it meant: 'And they said to E-l: Depart from us'—
אֵלּוּ הַיִּסּוּרִין שֶׁבָּאִים עַל יְדֵי שֵׁם זֶה.
these are the afflictions that come through this Name. "
וְדַעַת דְּרָכֶיךָ" – זֶה תּוֹרָה,
'And the knowledge of Your ways'—this is Torah,
הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
namely the Oral Torah;
שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב דְּרָכָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
for the Written Torah represents the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁהוּא מְקַיֵּים הַמִּצְווֹת תְּחִלָּה,
in that He fulfills the commandments first,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שָׁם וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (פֶּרֶק א דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הֲלָכָה ג),
as written in Midrash Rabbah there and in the Yerushalmi (Rosh Hashanah 1:3),
וְצִוָּונוּ לָלֶכֶת בִּדְרָכָיו וּלְקַיֵּים מִצְוֹתָיו וְחֻקָּיו.
and commanded us to walk in His ways and observe His commandments and statutes.
וְ"דַעַת דְּרָכֶיךָ" הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And 'the knowledge of Your ways' is the Oral Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י בְּפָרָשַׁת כִּי תִשָּׂא:
and as stated in Rashi's commentary in Parashat Ki Tisa: "
וּבְדַעַת" – רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ;
‘and in knowledge’—this is the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh);
וְהַיְינוּ רוּחַ מֵהַהוּא קֹדֶשׁ דִּלְעֵילָּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
namely a spirit drawn from that supernal Holiness, as stated in the holy Zohar.
וְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בָּאָה עַל יְדֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
And the Oral Torah comes through the Holy Spirit,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב.);
and as the Ramban wrote (Bava Batra 12a);
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ (מְגִילָּה יד:):
and so was expounded (Megillah 14b): "'
וַתִּלְבַּשׁ אֶסְתֵּר מַלְכוּת' – שֶׁלְּבָשַׁתְהוּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ",
‘"And Esther put on royal apparel"—that the Holy Spirit clothed her’,
וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
meaning the Oral Torah,
בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת, "פֶּה – תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה";
the aspect of Malchut: 'the mouth is the Oral Torah';
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי",
and concerning this it is stated: 'my speech shall distill as the dew',
וּפֵירֵשׁ הָרְקַנַאנְטִי (פָּרָשַׁת הַאֲזִינוּ) מִלְּשׁוֹן "בִּצַּע אֶמְרָתוֹ",
and the Recanati explained (Parashat Ha'azinu) from the root of 'He has performed His word',
דְּאָמְרִינַן בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה: "בָּזַע פּוּרְפִּירִין שֶׁלּוֹ",
as we say in the Midrash Rabbah: 'He tore His royal purple robe',
וְכֵן "אִמְרָתִי" – לְבוּשׁ מַלְכוּת שֶׁהוּא רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ;
and likewise 'imrati'—the royal garment which is the Holy Spirit;
וְזֶה שֶׁנִּקְרָא הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה "דַּעַת דְּרָכֶיךָ".
and this is why the Oral Torah is termed 'the knowledge of Your ways.'
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהָיָה אָז נֶפֶשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
And since the soul of Moses our teacher was present then,
וְהָיָה רָאוּי שֶׁתִּנָּתֵן תּוֹרָה עַל יָדוֹ לָהֶם
and it was fitting that Torah be given through him to them (
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג, רטז עַמּוּד ב),
(as stated in the holy Zohar Part III, 216b),
וְאָז הָיָה נִגְלֶה לָהֶם כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and then all of the Oral Torah would have been revealed to them
שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אֵצֶל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ.
which was enfolded within the Written Torah with Moses our teacher.
וְכֵן נִרְמַז בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נִבְקְעוּ כָּל מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה"
– And so it was hinted in the verse: 'all the fountains of the great deep burst open'—
מַבּוּעֵי דְּחָכְמְתָא לְתַתָּא,
the wellsprings of wisdom below,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קיז עַמּוּד א),
as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 117a),
שֶׁאִם הָיוּ רוֹצִים לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה
that had they willed to receive the Torah,
הָיָה נִגְלֶה לָהֶם כָּל הַחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
all lower wisdom, the Oral Torah, would have been revealed to them;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁזָּכוּ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
just as they merited at the Giving of the Torah through Moses our teacher,
דְּאִיתָא (נְדָרִים כב:):
for it is taught (Nedarim 22b):
אִלְמָלֵא חָטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא נִיתַּן לָהֶם אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי,
Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the Five Books of the Torah, etc.,
וְהָיָה כָּלוּל בָּהֶם כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and within them was enfolded the entire Oral Torah,
וְהָיוּ זוֹכִין לְהַשִּׂיג כָּל אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִתּוֹךְ הַתּוֹרָה;
and they would have merited to comprehend all the light of the Oral Torah directly from the Torah;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "וְדַעַת דְּרָכֶיךָ לֹא חָפָצְנוּ".
and this is what it meant: 'And the knowledge of Your ways we do not desire.'
וְקָאֵי גַּם כֵּן עַל שֵׁם "אֵל",
And this refers likewise to the Name E-l,
מַלְכוּת, "פֶּה – תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ".
Malchut: 'the mouth—we call it the Oral Torah.'
וְהַיְינוּ יִסּוּרִין לְתַקֵּן הֶעָבָר שֶׁבָּא מִמִּדָּה זוֹ,
Namely, afflictions to rectify the past which derive from this attribute,
דְּאִית דִּין וְאִית דַּיָּין;
that there is judgment and there is a Judge;
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לְתַקֵּן עַל לְהַבָּא,
and the Oral Torah to rectify for the future,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, רב עַמּוּד א):
as written (Zohar Part I, 202a): "
דְּהָא לֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְתַבְרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא",
‘for you have no word to shatter the evil inclination other than Torah’,
וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and this is the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סֻכָּה נב:):
as written (Sukkah 52b): "
אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ מְנֻוָּול זֶה מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ",
‘If this vile one confronts you, drag him to the study hall’,
וְהוּא מְקוֹם חִדּוּשׁ הֲלָכוֹת.
and that is the place where novel halakhot are innovated.
וּמִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה
And the Book of Deuteronomy (Mishneh Torah)
שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
which is from the root of the Oral Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, רסא עַמּוּד א);
as written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 261a);
וְכֵן נִכְתַּב בְּמִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה הַלּוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת
and so there was written in Deuteronomy the narrative of the Second Tablets
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן מִדְרָשׁ, הֲלָכוֹת וְאַגָּדוֹת,
which contain Midrash, Halakhot, and Aggadot,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מו);
as written (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 46);
וְכָל הַתּוֹכָחוֹת שֶׁבְּמִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה,
and all the admonitions in Deuteronomy,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף מְגִילָּה (לא:):
concerning which they said at the end of Megillah (31b): "
מֹשֶׁה מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ אֲמָרָן",
‘Moses spoke them from his own mouth’,
בְּכוּלָּם נִזְכַּר שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה,
in all of them the four-letter Name Havayah is mentioned,
שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הַיִּסּוּרִין רַק בְּרַחֲמִים
for in truth the afflictions stem solely from mercy,
לְהַפְחִיד הָאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה,
to arouse awe in man that he repent,
וּכְאָב דְּעָבֵיד נְהִימוּ סַגִּי,
like a father who roars loudly,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (תָּבוֹא).
and as written in the Zohar Chadash (Ki Tavo).
וְהֵם אָמְרוּ: "לָאֵל סוּר מִמֶּנּוּ",
Yet they said: 'To E-l: Depart from us,'
שֶׁאֵין רוֹצִים אַף בְּתַכְלִית יִסּוּרִין שֶׁהוּזְכְּרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (עֲרָכִין טז:).
refusing even the minimal measure of afflictions mentioned in the Gemara (Arachin 16b).
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם – יִסּוּרִין וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
– And both of them—afflictions and the Oral Torah—
מִשֵּׁם זֶה שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת מַלְכוּת.
derive from this Name, which is the attribute of Malchut.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 30:13: “Rabbi Acha said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to give them four things—Torah, suffering, sacrificial service, and prayer—but they did not want them. “They said to God, Depart from us”—this refers to suffering. “We do not desire knowledge of Your ways”—this is Torah. “What is the Almighty, that we should serve Him?”—these are the sacrifices. “What would we gain by entreating Him?”—this is prayer.”

וּבָאָרֶץ דְּאִקְרֵי כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and to the earth which is called the Congregation of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, לא סוֹף עַמּוּד א).
as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 31a end).
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ הַיִּחוּד עִם שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה שֶׁהוּא רַחֲמִים,
And since there is union with the Name Havayah which is mercy,
אֵין צָרִיךְ יִסּוּרִין לְכַפֵּר עַל הֶעָבָר,
afflictions are not required to atone for the past,
וְדַי בְּקָרְבָּנוֹת לְתַקֵּן כָּל הֶעָבָר;
and sacrifices suffice to rectify the entire past;
וְעַל לְהַבָּא גַּם כֵּן דַּי בִּתְפִלָּה
and for the future, prayer likewise suffices
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַעַזְרֵנוּ,
that Hashem, blessed be He, assist us,
שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזְרוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ,
for without the Holy One helping him, he could not overcome the inclination,
וְצָרִיךְ תְּפִלָּה עַל זֶה,
and prayer is required for this,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לח):
as written (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 38): "
קְחוּ עִמָּכֶם דְּבָרִים" – אֵין דְּבָרִים אֶלָּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,

וְהַיְינוּ לְתַקֵּן לְהַבָּא,
meaning to rectify for the future,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ מֵהַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and as we explained from the holy Zohar
דְּלֵית מִלָּה לְתַבְרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא;
that there is no word to break the evil inclination other than Torah;
אָמְרוּ לוֹ: "אֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין",
they said to Him: 'We do not know Torah',
אָמַר לָהֶם: "בְּכוּ וְהִתְפַּלְּלוּ לְפָנַי",
He said to them: 'Weep and pray before Me',
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל הָאָדָם לְפָנָיו
for Hashem desires that man pray before Him
וְלִקְרוֹתוֹ מִן הַמֵּצַר
and call unto Him from the straits
לַעֲזוֹר לוֹ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע,
to assist him in overcoming the evil inclination,
וְאָז ה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְּיָדוֹ.
and then Hashem will not leave him in its hand.
וְהֵם אָמְרוּ: "מַה שַּׁדַּי כִּי נַעַבְדֶנּוּ",
And they said: 'What is Shaddai that we should serve Him?'
שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ בְּקָרְבָּנוֹת לְתַקֵּן הֶעָבָר;
refusing sacrifices to rectify the past; "
וּמַה נּוֹעִיל כִּי נִפְגַּע בּוֹ"
– 'And what profit should we have if we pray to Him?'—
שֶׁאָמְרוּ כֵּיוָן שֶׁמָּסַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הַבְּחִירָה לָאָדָם,
arguing that since the Holy One granted free will to man,
לֹא יוֹעִיל תְּפִלָּה לְהִנָּצֵל מִקִּטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע.
prayer will not avail to be saved from the accusation of the evil inclination.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 38:4: “Another matter: “This is the matter” – that is what is written: “Take words with you” (Hosea 14:3). That is what the verse said: “I wash my hands in purity, [and I circle Your altar, Lord], sounding a voice of thanksgiving” (Psalms 26:6–7). Is it, perhaps, to sacrifice bulls and rams? The verse states: “Sounding a voice of thanksgiving.” Because Israel said: Master of the universe, the princes sin, they bring an offering, and it is atoned for them; the anointed sins, he brings an offering, and it is atoned for him. We do not have an offering. He said to them: “If the entire congregation of Israel shall err unwittingly.… [they shall bring a young bull as a sin offering]” (Leviticus 4:13–14). They said to Him: We are poor, and we do not have the means to bring offerings. He said to them: I am seeking words, as it is stated: “Take words with you and return to the Lord” (Hosea 14:3), and I will forgive all your sins. “Words” are nothing other than words of Torah, as it is stated: “These are the words that Moses spoke” (Deuteronomy 1:1). They said to Him: But we do not know. He said to them: Weep and pray before Me, and I will accept it. When your ancestors were enslaved in Egypt, was it not through prayer that I redeemed them, as it is stated: “The children of Israel groaned due to the work, and they cried out” (Exodus 2:23)? In the days of Joshua, was it not through prayer that I performed miracles on their behalf, as it is stated: “Joshua rent his garments” (Joshua 7:6)? What did I say to him: “Extend the javelin” (Joshua 8:18). In the days of the Judges, through weeping I heard their cry, as it is stated: “It was when the children of Israel cried to the Lord” (Judges 6:7). In the days of Samuel, was it not through prayer that I heard them, as it is stated: “Samuel called out to the Lord on behalf of Israel, and the Lord answered him (I Samuel 7:9)? Likewise, the people of Jerusalem, even though they angered Me, because they wept, I had mercy on them, as it is stated: “For so said the Lord: Sing with joy for Jacob, and exult.… [they will come with weeping and supplications] (Jeremiah 31:6–8). That is, I ask of you neither sacrifices nor offerings, but rather, words, as it is stated: “Take words with you and return to the Lord” (Hosea 14:3). That is why David said: “I wash my hands in purity” (Psalms 26:6). He does not say: “To sacrifice to you” but rather, “sounding a voice of thanksgiving” (Psalms 26:7), that I thank you for the words of Torah. Another matter: “Take words with you” (Hosea 14:3) – Moses said: “The abode of the God of eternity” (Deuteronomy 33:27), this is Israel, as by their merit the world was created and upon them the world stands. Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says: “He drove the enemy away from before you” (Deuteronomy 33:27) – this is Haman, as it is stated: “[Esther said:] A man who is an adversary and an enemy, [this evil Haman]” (Esther 7:6). Why “an adversary and an enemy”? An adversary [to God] above and an enemy [to Israel] below; an adversary to the fathers and an enemy to the children; an adversary to me and an enemy to you. “And He said: Destroy” (Deuteronomy 33:27) – these are his sons. “Israel dwelled securely, alone is the spring [ein] of Jacob” (Deuteronomy 33:28) – ein is nothing other than prophecy, as it is stated: “For the Lord poured upon you a spirit of deep sleep and He closed your eyes [eineikhem]; [He covered the prophets]” (Isaiah 29:10). Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel said: Great is [God’s] love of Israel, as the Holy One blessed be He changes the law of nature for their benefit, as He rains manna for them from the heavens and causes dew to rise for them from the ground, as it is stated: “The layer of dew lifted” (Exodus 16:14), and likewise, “His heavens drip dew” (Deuteronomy 33:28). When Moses saw the reward given to the righteous, he said to them: “Happy are you, Israel; who is like you, a people saved by the Lord” (Deuteronomy 33:29), people who are served by the Holy One blessed be He. “The shield [magen] of your assistance” (Deuteronomy 33:29) – corresponding to Abraham, as it is stated: “Who delivered [migen] your adversaries into your hand” (Genesis 14:20). “And who is the sword of your honor” (Deuteronomy 33:29) – corresponding to Isaac, who extended his neck to the sword. “Your enemies will seek to deceive you” (Deuteronomy 33:29) – corresponding to Jacob, as it is stated: “And went to a land, due to his brother Jacob” (Genesis 36:6). “And you will tread on their high places” (Deuteronomy 33:29) – in the days of Mordekhai, as it is stated: “Haman took the garments and the horse” (Esther 6:11). What caused Mordekhai to achieve this greatness? Say it is because he would constantly pray, as it is stated: “Mordekhai knew everything that was done […and cried a loud and bitter cry]” (Esther 4:1). Even after he saw himself achieve prominence, he never became haughty and never ceased from prayer, but rather, “Mordekhai returned” (Esther 6:12), just as he was initially. “The Lord your God will place all these curses” (Deuteronomy 30:7), not on you, but “on your enemies, and on those who hate you, who pursued you” (Deuteronomy 30:7). And will you cease from prayer? No, but rather, what is written thereafter: “You will return and heed the voice of the Lord” (Deuteronomy 30:8), just as Mordekhai did, as it is stated: “Mordekhai returned to the king’s gate” (Esther 6:12), as he returned to his sackcloth and his fasting. That is why it is stated: “Take words with you” (Hosea 14:3). Here, too, it says: “This is the matter,” because the Holy One blessed be He acceded to Aaron only through prayer, as it is stated: “The Lord was incensed with Aaron to destroy him, [and I prayed on behalf of Aaron, as well, at that time]” (Deuteronomy 9:20).”

h: Moshe, the Divine Names, and the Gift of Shabbat

p: וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי גִּימַטְרִיָּא שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת אֵלּוּ מֹשֶׁה,
And for this reason the gematria of these two Names (E-l + Shaddai = 31 + 314 = 345) is Moshe,
שֶׁחֶלְקוֹ הָיָה הַשַּׁבָּת,
whose allotted portion was Shabbat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יִשְׂמַח מֹשֶׁה בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ",
as written: 'Moses rejoiced in the gift of his portion',
שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ תָּמִיד הַיִּחוּד.
for with him the divine union was constant.
וּכְמוֹ דִּבְשַׁבָּת שֶׁהַיִּשְׂרָאֵל כָּל הַיּוֹם כְּעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה,
And just as on Shabbat an Israelite is considered the entire day as performing a mitzvah,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁמּוּרְגָּל בִּמְלָאכָה תָּמִיד
since he is always accustomed to labor
וּפוֹרֵשׁ בִּשְׁבִיל קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת,
yet desists for the sake of the sanctity of Shabbat,
הֲוָה לֵיהּ כָּל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת כְּבָא לְיָדוֹ דְּבַר עֲבֵירָה וְנִיצּוֹל הֵימֶנָּה
his entire Sabbath day is like one confronted with sin who is saved from it,
שֶׁחָשׁוּב כְּעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה
which is credited as performing a positive mitzvah (
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר קִדּוּשִׁין לט:);
(as stated in Kiddushin 39b);
וְכָל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת הוּא יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ
and the entire Sabbath day is the union of the Holy One and His Shekhinah,
כְּמוֹ בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיַּת מִצְוָה.
just as at the moment of performing a commandment.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ בְּכָל הַיָּמִים הַיִּחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ,
And with Moses our teacher the union of the Holy One and His Shekhinah occurred continuously on all days,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ",
and as it is written: 'And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him',
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלָּקַח עִמּוֹ עֶצֶם קְדוּשַׁת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק
meaning that he took with him the essence of the holiness of Joseph the Righteous,
שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם וְשֵׁם שֶׁלּוֹ;
who is the Chariot for the attribute of the Righteous One, Foundation of the World, and His Name;

h: Shabbat Humility and the Rectification of the Week

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת נַעֲשָׂה הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל עָנִי וּנְכֵה רוּחַ
And on Shabbat a Jew becomes humble and contrite of spirit
כְּשֶׁחוֹשֵׁב כָּל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלָיו בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
when he reflects upon everything that passed over him during the workdays,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פָּסוּק זֶה עַל הַשַּׁבָּת.
as we explained regarding the verse cited at the start of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah applying this to Shabbat.
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ יִסּוּרִין,
And he does not require physical afflictions,
שֶׁנּוֹפֵל עָלָיו הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה,
for dread and awe fall upon him,
וְדַי בִּנְהִימוּ סַגִּי שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה נְכֵה רוּחַ,
and a great groan suffices to render him contrite of spirit,
וְנִשְׁבַּר לִבּוֹ בְּקִרְבּוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה מִפַּחַד ה'.
and his heart breaks within him and he repents out of fear of Hashem.
וְכֵן זוֹכֶה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
And likewise he merits words of Torah, the Written Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְדִכְכוּלֵי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל";
as stated: 'and all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given to Israel';
וְכֵן הוּא זְמַן לִזְכּוֹת לְהַשְׁפָּעָה בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and likewise it is the time to merit an influx into the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, מז עַמּוּד ב):
as stated (Zohar Part I, 47b): "
יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי – דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכוּלֵי".
‘the seventh day—this is the Oral Torah, etc.’
וְכֵן זוֹכִין לְקָרְבָּנוֹת,
And likewise we merit sacrifices,
שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "וְאֶת מוּסַף יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה נַעֲשֶׂה וְנַקְרִיב לְפָנֶיךָ בְּאַהֲבָה",
for we recite: 'And the additional offering of this Sabbath day we shall prepare and sacrifice before You in love',
וְאָמַרְנוּ דְּאַף שֶׁאֵין מַקְרִיבִין מוּסָף בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה,
and we explained that even though we do not offer the Musaf in this era,
וַאֲפִילּוּ אִם יִבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא נוּכַל גַּם כֵּן לְהַקְרִיב תֵּיכֶף מוּסָף זֶה,
and even if the Temple were rebuilt right now we could not immediately sacrifice this specific Musaf,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹצִים לְהַקְרִיב רַק אֲנוּסִים אֲנַחְנוּ מֵחֲמַת חֶסְרוֹן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וּמִזְבֵּחַ,
nonetheless, since we desire to offer it and are prevented solely due to the lack of the Temple and Altar,
וְחִשֵּׁב לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה וְלֹא עֲשָׂאָהּ מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאָהּ
and 'one who intended to do a mitzvah and was prevented, Scripture credits him as though he did it' (
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם מ.),
(as stated in the Gemara there, Kiddushin 40a),
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ כָּאן "וּנְשַׁלְּמָה פָרִים שְׂפָתֵינוּ",
and all the more so since here applies 'so will we render the calves of our lips',
וְחָשׁוּב כְּאִילּוּ מַקְרִיבִין הַמּוּסָף עַל יְדֵי הָאַהֲבָה וְחֵשֶׁק לַעֲשׂוֹת.
and it is credited as though we offered the Musaf through the love and desire to perform it.
וְכֵן תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת עִיקַּר הַתְּפִלָּה:
And so too prayer, for on Shabbat the core of prayer is: "
קַדְּשֵׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ וְתֵן חֶלְקֵנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ וְטַהֵר לִבֵּנוּ לְעָבְדְּךָ בֶּאֱמֶת",
‘Sanctify us with Your commandments, and grant our portion in Your Torah, and purify our hearts to serve You in truth’,
וְאֵין מִתְפַּלְּלִין כְּלָל עַל צָרְכֵי הַגּוּף
and we do not pray at all for physical bodily needs,
רַק עַל צָרְכֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
only for spiritual needs of the soul,
לִזְכּוֹת לְטָהֳרַת הַלֵּב וּלְהִנָּצֵל מִקִּטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
to merit purity of heart and to be spared from the accusation of the evil inclination.
וְזוֹ הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ לִיתֵּן לְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל לְהוֹעִיל לְהַבָּא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
And this is the prayer He sought to give the Generation of the Flood to avail for the future, as we explained.
וְזוֹכִין בְּשַׁבָּת לְכָל הָאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל לְקַבֵּל,
And on Shabbat we merit all four things that the Generation of the Flood refused to accept,
וְהַזְּמַן בְּשַׁבָּת לִזְכּוֹת לְתַקֵּן כָּל פְּגַם דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל,
and the time on Shabbat is propitious to merit rectifying the entire blemish of the Flood generation,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם לְתַקֵּן,
which is the root blemish of the Serpent which they were tasked to rectify,
וּבְשַׁבָּת יְכוֹלִים לִזְכּוֹת לְתַקֵּן.
and on Shabbat we are empowered to merit its rectification.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 50:2: “For when Hashem hears his cry, he is remembered before Him, and consequently, “you shall be saved from your enemies”—the evil inclination, which is called an enemy, as they said in Sukkah 52a. The evil inclination's entire power to hold the depths of the heart comes through forgetfulness. Although the root of the heart is always attached to Hashem, it nevertheless causes this to be entirely forgotten, until all the thoughts of the heart are wholly evil, God forbid, and sin has left a stain through and through. But when he is remembered before Hashem, remembrance is also awakened in his heart, so that he remembers Hashem. Consequently, the barrier of forgetfulness within his heart is broken, and he can bring his hidden Jewish root into the open, until, little by little, he reaches full recognition and complete repentance.”
